newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The draft constitution may ease the "iron rule" of the current version requiring the prime minister to be a member of parliament by allowing a non-elected person to become the top national executive. Ironically, the "iron rule" has been imposed shortly after the May 1992 bloody military crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators who demanded that the then prime minister, General Suchinda Kraprayoon, step down because he had not been elected by the people. (BANGKOK POST)

- Army chief General Chettha Thanajaro is hopeful that his talks today with his Burmese counterpart General Maung Aye, the first between the current army commanders of the two countries, will help resolve a number of border problems and pave the way for an official visit to Burma by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. (THE NATION)

- Authorities will inspect high-rises throughout the city to ensure they are well-equipped with fire safety systems in a bid to avert further disasters in the wake of the President Tower blaze. Bangkok Governor Bhichit Rattakul says he will order a special team of officials to make fire safety inspections at high-rises, especially ones built before the Building Control Act 1992 took effect. He says he will also lobby the Interior Ministry to issue a regulation requiring buildings constructed before 1992 to have fire safety systems installed. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand has granted Sri Dhana Finance and Securities permission to close operations for four days after the company's new head office was destroyed in Sunday's fire at President Tower. Damage to the seventh-floor office was estimated at 40 million baht, but vital documents, promissory notes and bills of exchange remained intact in the company safe. Other important information was saved on hard disks not yet at the office. (BANGKOK POST)

- Regulations to set up the second national airline may be revised to make the operation more attractive in the case of zero interest being shown for the present round of applications. The Aviation Department yesterday - the last day open for applications - distributed the bidding terms of reference to parties interested in establishing up the airline. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thailand plans to join with other ASEAN members to send a letter to the U.S. trade representative, urging the U.S. not to promote ASEAN countries out of tariff concessions when Washington reviews the scheme in May. Officials say Thailand appears to be highest on the list of recipient countries likely to be phased out of the generalised system of preferences programme. (THE NATION)
